questions.def: Future perfect expresses completion before a future time.
questions.question: By the time the report is due, I ___ all the data.

questions.def: Present perfect indicates an action completed recently.
questions.question: The research team ___ significant progress lately.

questions.def: Present perfect continuous for duration up to now.
questions.question: I ___ in this city for over a decade.

questions.def: Future perfect emphasizes completion before a future time.
questions.question: They ___ their research by the end of next year.

questions.def: Past participle is needed after 'Having' in perfect participle phrases.
questions.question: Having ___ the experiment, they published the results.

questions.def: Past perfect is correct with 'by the time' for a completed action.
questions.question: By the time she arrived, the presentation had already started.

questions.def: Past perfect clarifies one action before another in the past.
questions.question: She ___ diligently before the exam.

questions.def: 'Had barely' shows an action completed just before another.
questions.question: He ___ finished the assignment when the deadline arrived.

questions.def: Past perfect expresses regret about a past action.
questions.question: I wish I ___ harder in school.

questions.def: Past perfect defines completed actions before a past time.
questions.question: By then, she ___ three novels.

questions.def: 'Having finished' is correct perfect participle construction.
questions.question: ___ the report, I submitted it immediately.

questions.def: Past perfect emphasizes a prior expectation in the past.
questions.question: They ___ expected such a positive outcome.

questions.def: Future perfect is correct for a completed future action.
questions.question: By next summer, they ___ to Europe.

questions.def: 'Should have' expresses regret or criticism in the past.
questions.question: She ___ been more careful with the data.

questions.def: Past perfect is used after 'as if' for unreal past situations.
questions.question: He acted as if he ___ the news before.

questions.def: Past perfect shows completion before a specific past time.
questions.question: They ___ the project before the deadline.

questions.def: Past perfect emphasizes the completion of the rain.
questions.question: It ___ raining before I left home.

questions.def: Past perfect is needed with 'never' to emphasize prior experience.
questions.question: We ___ never experienced such a thing.

questions.def: Present perfect continuous for an ongoing action.
questions.question: I ___ for you for an hour.

questions.def: Future perfect for completion before future time.
questions.question: By the time he graduates, he ___ four years.

questions.def: Past participle after 'Having' for perfect participle construction.
questions.question: Having ___ the data, they began analysis.

questions.def: Present perfect continuous for ongoing action.
questions.question: She ___ on the project for months.

questions.def: Past perfect expresses an unrealized past expectation.
questions.question: We ___ expected such a result.

questions.def: Past perfect expresses regret for past actions.
questions.question: I wish I ___ that mistake.

questions.def: Future perfect indicates completion before a future point.
questions.question: By the time the negotiations conclude, we ___ all avenues.

questions.def: Past perfect continuous emphasizes duration before a past event.
questions.question: The research team ___ the data meticulously for months before publishing.

questions.def: Past perfect shows completion before another past action.
questions.question: The author ___ extensively on the subject before her death.

questions.def: Past perfect expresses a hope unfulfilled by a past event.
questions.question: They ___ to finish the project by the deadline, despite the challenges.

questions.def: Future perfect for completion before a future time.
questions.question: By next year, she ___ her doctorate.

questions.def: Present perfect continuous for activity up to now.
questions.question: He ___ tirelessly on the manuscript for months.
